metadata.title: UAE generalised geology zones — Phase 1 v0.1 approximation
metadata.data_origin: Hand-digitised polygons approximated from cited academic literature — NOT precision GIS
metadata.intended_use: Coarse-zoom (city-scale) Mole Agent context layer; replace with USGS geo2bg shapefile (DOI 10.5066/P9GI9NS4, public domain) once direct download path is unblocked
metadata.licence: CC0 — derived from public-domain academic descriptions
citations: Alsharhan & Kendall (2003) — coastal sabkha extent description, Geology of the Arabian Peninsula
IJERA Vol 5 Issue 6 — Geotechnical properties of Sabkha soil, southern UAE — https://www.ijera.com/papers/Vol5_issue6/Part%20-%203/E56032429.pdf
Springer Discover Sustainability 2025 — Sabkha soils Abu Dhabi Metropolitan — https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s43621-025-01187-9
USGS Open-File Report 97-470B — Maps showing geology of the Arabian Peninsula (referenced for regional structure) — https://pubs.usgs.gov/publication/ofr97470B

schema.zone_type: one of: COASTAL_SABKHA | INTERIOR_SABKHA | RUB_AL_KHALI_DUNES | HAJAR_OPHIOLITE | COASTAL_SAND | URBAN_INFILL
schema.foundation_risk: one of: LOW | MEDIUM | HIGH | CRITICAL
schema.source: cited academic source for the polygon
schema.precision: always APPROXIMATE in v0.1; replace with USGS geo2bg in v0.2

properties.name: Abu Dhabi → Umm Al Quwain coastal sabkha belt
properties.description: Coastal sabkha extending ~24 km inland between Abu Dhabi and Umm Al Quwain per Alsharhan & Kendall (2003). Hypersaline, brine-saturated silt+sand; foundation cost penalty 30-60% via piles + dewatering.
properties.source: Alsharhan & Kendall (2003) + IJERA UAE sabkha properties

properties.name: Sabkhat Matti (northern Rub Al Khali)
properties.description: Largest UAE sabkha; extends ~150 km in northern Rub Al Khali per Alsharhan & Kendall (2003). Major foundation-cost driver for any deep development; specialist geotechnical investigation mandatory.

properties.name: Rub Al Khali sand dune system (UAE portion)
properties.description: Aeolian sand dunes covering southern Abu Dhabi emirate. Bearing capacity acceptable for shallow foundations; deep foundations OK but require careful liquefaction analysis under seismic loading.
properties.source: Springer 2018 ME geotechnical review + general UAE geology context

properties.name: Hajar Mountains ophiolite (eastern UAE — Fujairah / Ras Al Khaimah)
properties.description: Cretaceous Semail Ophiolite — peridotite + gabbro bedrock at or near surface. Excellent bearing capacity; rock-anchored foundations standard.
properties.source: USGS OFR 97-470B regional + general UAE geology

properties.name: Dubai + northern Emirates coastal sand (developable)
properties.description: Quaternary coastal sand + sabkha-margin transition. Most Dubai urban development sits here; standard pile + raft foundations work with site-specific groundwater + bearing investigation.
properties.source: Synthesised from Dubai borehole data (groundwater 4.5-4.6m typical)
